recipes.name: Jim's Beer-Battered Portobello Mushrooms
ingredients_raw: 2 cups bitter ale (such as Goose Island Honkers Ale®)
3 large portobello mushroom caps, cut into 1/2-inch slices

steps.text: Heat oil in a deep fryer or large saucepan to 375 degrees F (190 degrees C).
Whisk ale, flour, sesame seeds, cornstarch, and baking powder together in a large bowl; batter will be thick and slightly lumpy.
Dip mushroom strips into batter, 7 to 8 at a time; shake off excess.
Lower mushroom strips carefully into the hot oil in batches. Fry until golden brown, 5 to 6 minutes. Transfer to a paper towel-lined plate to drain. Repeat with remaining mushroom strips.

raw_recipe.headline: Jim's Beer-Battered Portobello Mushrooms
raw_recipe.description: Jim's beer-battered portobello mushroom recipe calls for dipping portobello mushroom strips in beer batter and deep-frying them until they're crunchy.

review.reviewBody: I used baby porobello's and did not cut them. The taste was awesome, Husband say's I should half them. Even still he made me take the plate away because he could not stop eating them. I also used the batter to make the broccoli for fried Friday and Hubby ate more then half of the veggies.

OH MY GOSH!!! These are the BEST fried mushrooms we have ever had in our life. We absolutely loved them, they were fabulous! I'm making them again tonight. Thank you so much for this delicious recipe!

I made this recipe, it was good. My family liked it alot but there are things I would change. For example like someone said, it is too bland I would add onion powder garlic powder salt pepper or even Worcestershire sauce. Also this recipe calls for for bitter ale and that is probably pretty important don't use sour types of drinks. For my taste there were too many sesame seeds it made it bitter. Also since you're supposed to deep fry these they tasted really heavy I would recommend some sort of vinegary or savory/sweet sauce. And one last thing, if you like the taste of mushrooms cut them pretty thick like about one centimeter because they shrink quite a bit and the flavor gets a little lost.

These were totally delicious and we will definitely have them again and again. We do Keto most of the time so I used these instead of potatoes last time I grilled steak. I used coconut and almond flour instead of wheat flour and Heinekin light beer which still has the very hoppy flavor but lots less carbs. Great recipe! Thanks for sharing!

made this tonight. batter was super easy but bland. when I added garlic salt, onion powder, smoked Spanish paprika and a hint of cayenne pepper it made it so much better. we used whole baby Portabella mushrooms to make it easier on cooking.
